Committee: Education Policy
Sponsor: Rich
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 02/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 260 as introduced could increase obligations of local boards of education by an undetermined amount to provide certain assurances to teachers; and to require a copy of the Teacher Bill of Rights, established by this bill, to be (1) provided to teachers, and parents or legal guardians; (2) posted in schools and administrative buildings; and (3) displayed on school and local board of education websites.
In addition, this bill would require the Paperwork Reduction Committee to convene within 15 days after the effective date of this act and report any findings and recommendations to the State Superintendent of Education by December 1, 2021, for presentation to the Legislative Council by the first day of the 2022 Regular Session, which could increase the obligations of the State Department of Education by an undetermined amount dependent upon assistance provided to the Committee.
Terri Collins, Chair
Education Policy

Committee: Financial Services
Sponsor: Lipscomb
Analyst: Julie Knight
Date: 02/19/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 198 as introduced clarifies the calculation of taxable income for credit unions under the Alabama financial institution excise tax law. Otherwise, this bill will not directly affect state or local funding.
Chris Blackshear, Chair
Financial Services
